 ORDER IN WP NO. 22435/2022:-
In this writ petition, the petitioner is assailing the order dated 05.04.2022 passed by respondent No.2 herein in RRT (THA)35/2022-23 (Annexure-B1).
2.

3. Perusal of the writ petition would indicate that the said order is challenged before respondent No.1 herein as per Annexure-C dated 05.05.2022 to the writ petition.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3 that, respondent No.1 herein has NC: 2023:KHC:40761 disposed of the appeal preferred by the petitioner herein under Section 136(2) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act in RA No.292/2022 dated 14.03.2023.
In that view of the matter, reserving liberty to the petitioner to challenge the same before the competent authority, WP No.22435/2022 is disposed of.

5. All the contentions of the parties are kept open and the period spent by the petitioner before this Court be condoned, if the Revision Petition is preferred before the competent authority, within six (06) months from the receipt of this order.

IN WP NO. 2100/2023:-
In this writ petition, petitioners have assailed the order dated 22.08.2022, passed by respondent No.2 in RA No.271/2022 (Annexure-D) and interalia have sought for direction to the respondent-authorities to restore the mutation entries in MR H 47/2020-21 in favour of the petitioners as it was in existence in respect of the land bearing Survey No.121/1F, measuring 0-05 Guntas, NC: 2023:KHC:40761 situated at Bogadi Village, Kasaba Hobli, Mysuru Taluk (for short 'the land in question') before the proceedings in RA No.271/2022 dated 22.08.2022 (Annexure-D).
2.

The relevant facts for adjudication of the writ petition are that, the petitioners claim to be the owners in possession of the land bearing Survey No.159 (new Survey No.121), measuring 5 Acres 5 Guntas, situated at Bogadi Village, Mysore Taluk.

It is stated in the writ petition that, the land in question was auctioned by the competent Civil Court in favour of one Basavaiah, resident of Bogadi Village and one Linga,
resident of Kukkarahalli Village, as per the registered sale deed dated 01.06.1911.
Thereafter, the petitioners herein have purchased the very same land as per the registered sale deed dated 17.03.1964 produced at Annexure-A series to the writ petition.

3. It is the grievance of the petitioners that, respondent No.1, taking advantage of the similarity of the NC: 2023:KHC:40761 names of the father of petitioner No.1, has changed the mutation in MR H-47/2020-21 in respect of the land in question.
4.

It is contended by the contesting respondents herein before respondent No.2 that, the father of the petitioners herein, on fictitious documents, have challenged MR H-47/2020-21 and in the said proceedings, respondent No.2 has allowed the appeal on 22.08.2022 (Annexure-D) to the writ petition.

5. It is also forthcoming in the writ petition that, the petitioners herein have filed WP No.37660/2017 and connected WP No.41384/2017 before this Court seeking relief of declaration L Basavaraju vs N Lingaiah on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14419517/
4

that the acquisition proceedings initiated by the Mysore Urban Development Authority, Mysore,
have become lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: This Court, as per the order dated 03.07.2019 (Annexure-F4), quashed the acquisition proceedings NC: 2023:KHC:40761 initiated by the respondent-Mysore Urban Development Authority and the land was restored in the name of the petitioners herein.
In that view of the matter, it is contended by the petitioners herein that,
respondent

No.2 herein, without considering the factual aspects on record and without extending fair opportunity of hearing to the petitioners, has passed the impugned order which requires interference with this writ petition.

6. I have heard Sri Shivaramu H.C, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Sri Subrahmanya Kaushik B.S, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri Mohammed Jaffar Shah, the learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent Nos.2 to 5.
7.

Sri Shivaramu H.C, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, invited the attention of this Court to order passed by this Court in WP No.37660/2017 and connected matter WP No.41384/2017 as well as the order NC: 2023:KHC:40761 sheet maintained by respondent No.2 herein produced at Annexure-C and contended that, without issuing notice to the petitioners herein,
respondent No.2 herein has passed the order, which requires to be interfered with by this Court.

He also contended that, the suit filed by the contesting respondents herein in OS No.676/2007 seeking relief of declaration is pending consideration before the Small Causes Court, Mysuru and in that view of the matter, unless the contesting respondents herein substantiate their rights in respect of the land in question, respondent No.2 herein ought not to have passed the impugned order,
changing the mutation entry in favour of the contesting respondents herein.
Accordingly, he sought for interference of this Court.

8. Per-contra, Sri Subrahmanya Kaushik B.S, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1,
has not disputed the submission with regard to the pendency of the suit filed by the contesting respondents in O.S.No.676/2007, however, sought to justify the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40761 impugned order on the ground that, the order passed by respondent No.2 herein is based on the decree in O.S.No.534/2005 and therefore, contended that, no interference is called for in this writ petition.

9. Sri. Mohammed jaffar shah, learned Additional Government Advocate sought to justify the impugned order and also raised the plea relating to the maintainability of the petition on the ground that, the petitioners are having efficacious remedy under the provisions of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act.

11. In the light of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, a careful examination of the writ papers would indicate that, the petitioners herein have filed WP No.37660/2017 and connected WP No.41384/2017, seeking quashing of the notification issued by L Basavaraju vs N Lingaiah on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14419517/
5 the respondents herein, acquiring the land in question in favour of the Mysore Urban Development Authority, Mysore.

This Court by order dated 03.07.2019 (Annexure-F4), quashed the impugned - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40761 notification therein passed by the respondent-authorities seeking acquisition of the land in question.
It is also forthcoming from the writ petition that, the mutation entry has been made in MR H-47/2020-21, which is based on the IHC proceedings by the respondent-authorities.
However, based on the decree passed by the Civil Court in O.S.No.534/2005, respondent No.2 has modified the mutation entry and made it in favour of the contesting respondents herein.
undisputably, the suit in O.S.No.534/2005 is filed seeking permanent injunction against the petitioners herein.

That apart, it is submitted that O.S.No.676/2007 is filed by the contesting respondents herein, seeking declarative relief from the competent Court and the said suit is pending consideration before the competent Court and therefore, I am of the view that, the parties have to establish their rights in the said suit.
Therefore, I am of the view that the change of the mutation by respondent No.2 herein, based on the decree in O.S.No.534/2005 is not correct as the said suit is filed seeking relief of injunction.
The contesting - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40761 respondents herein have to establish their rights with respect to the land in question in O.S.No.676/2007.

In that view of the matter, though the learned counsel appearing for the contesting respondents raised the plea with regard to alternative remedy, however, a careful examination of the order sheet maintained by respondent No.2 would indicate that, no notice has been issued to the petitioners herein before passing the impugned order.

In that view of the matter,
I pass the following:
ORDER i. The writ petition is allowed.
ii. Order dated 22.08.2022 (Annexure-D) passed by respondent No.2 is set aside.
iii. Parties are directed to establish their rights in O.S.No.676/2007 pending consideration before the competent Court.
iv.
In the meanwhile, respondent No.3 herein is directed to restore the original mutation register as per MR H-47/2020-21 in favour of the petitioners herein.
Consequent upon allowing the writ petition, quashing the mutation order dated 05.09.2022 (Annexure-G) in MR No.T18, does not arise.
vi. Order dated 24.09.2022 (Annexure-H) passed by respondent No.4 is set aside.
